# PR #259 performance verdict

**PASS** at `d4ed02aabdb7989508f3205307ded9927f76a694`.
Request: `01a1f259-27e7-70c3-a543-da067f59e127`.

No performance blocker found. The real-SDK registration canary is an on-demand check, not a new resident loop or per-seat hook.

## Executed proof

Verified the detached review worktree's full HEAD and read the complete PR diff, canary parent/loader, real extension startup and native-host ancestry traversal. `just worktree-deps --check` reported READY; no dependency install was needed.

Ran, in the review worktree:

```sh
/usr/bin/nice -n 19 /usr/bin/time -lp just copilot-sdk-contract --json
```

Exit **0**, report **pass**, installed and verified SDK version **1.0.114-0**, **7/7 checks passed**. Real **0.21 s**, user **0.15 s**, system **0.04 s**. `time -l` reported maximum resident set size **58,408,960 bytes**; this is its command resource statistic, not a measured sum of concurrent child RSS.

Then ran the same niced recipe once with a temporary Node preload that logged child_process launch calls, preserving execFile's custom promisify behavior and otherwise forwarding calls unchanged. It passed **7/7** again. Observed launch sites:

| Parent | API and program | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Canary driver | execFile `copilot --version` | 1 |
| Canary driver | spawn absolute `process.execPath` with the real extension and SDK loader | 1 |
| Real extension child | execFile `ps -p <driver> -o pid=,ppid=,comm=` | 1 |
| Real extension child | execFile `ps -p <driver> -o lstart=` | 1 |

Thus **four child-launch calls**, matching the stated normal-run claim, plus the driver Node process started by the recipe itself; shell/just/nice launch overhead is not included in that four. The installed copilot launcher was itself a Node process in the observer trace. No other child_process launch calls were recorded in the instrumented processes. The outer requested nice and recipe's own nice compose to 20 on this Mac, inherited by driver/CLI/extension; this is more conservative priority, not an un-niced test or a hot-path change.

The preload changed no repository file, SDK shape, handler or protocol and is removed after use. This was process-launch observation, not an OS-wide accounting of every exec/fork performed by native code.

## Rate, scaling and lifecycle

- **Idle cost: zero.** No daemon, status line, timer, pane hook or seat receiver calls the canary. Runtime call-site search (including hidden source trees) finds only `just doctor`, `just self-check` and the explicit `harness checks` sensor. `just install` calls doctor once as bootstrap, not per tick.
- `harness checks` invokes each sensor once through its existing finite sequential SENSORS loop; `copilot-sdk` is not a watched/background sensor registration. A user who manually runs a complete gate twice pays twice; there is no hidden seat-count multiplier.
- **On-demand normal cost: one driver Node plus the four observed child launches per invocation, 0.21 s on this run.** At R invocations/s, the observed child-launch contribution is 4R/s, not a fixed fleet polling rate. No benchmark throughput claim is made from one run.
- The version subprocess is capped at 10 s; protocol waits are per-step 10 s deadlines. The extension child is explicitly closed and awaited, with a 3 s SIGKILL fallback, and its temporary state directory is removed. No long-lived process is introduced.
- **Absolute paths:** the new extension-child spawn uses `process.execPath`. Version discovery is `COPILOT_BIN` or one PATH lookup of `copilot`. The two existing real-extension probes use bare `ps`; they are not changed by this PR and are observed only in this finite canary startup, not added to a repeated daemon path. No new daemon launch site exists; `spawn_sites.rs` is unaffected.
- **Proof limit on the advertised two ps calls:** two were observed, but they are not a formal upper bound. `resolveNativeHost` can inspect up to 64 ancestors and confirm a host, with two ps calls per inspection. This canary normally closes the child before a further walk. Do not copy the observed count into an assertion that all future SDK schedules must launch exactly two ps processes; an extended startup could do additional bounded ancestry probes. There is still no polling/per-seat rate here.

The loader's recursive config wrapping is bounded by the extension's small in-memory config and runs once. RPC parsing and handler/event checks run only for this invocation; no new steady-state computation is added to the product.

## Verification boundary

The direct run exercises the installed SDK against the real extension at the exact requested head. CI statuses at that head are green; CI without Copilot cannot prove installed-SDK behavior and was not substituted for the direct run. No local builds, cargo, full gates, --record writes, daemon bounce or live-seat mutation ran. No controlled fleet-wide before/after improvement is claimed for a 0.21-second on-demand command.
